How to choose a smartwatch that works with your phone

Phone compatibility comes before the price or the number of advertised features. A bargain watch is poor value if it cannot pair with your phone or use the features you need.

iPhone or Android: check the exact watch and software

Apple publishes a compatibility table covering the watch model, iPhone and software. For an older or refurbished watch, check its installed watchOS as well as the model: updated software can change the iPhone requirements. Source: Apple’s compatibility table.

Google says Pixel Watch 2 needs Android 9.0 or newer and does not support iPhones. Other generations have different minimums. Source: Google’s Pixel Watch compatibility guidance. Check each Samsung or other-brand model separately rather than assuming all Android watches have the same requirements.

Bluetooth vs cellular: decide what you need away from your phone

Bluetooth and cellular variants are not interchangeable offers. If you want calls or data without carrying your phone, check the exact LTE model, regional support, carrier compatibility and ongoing plan cost. Do not pay for cellular hardware if your usual use is with the phone nearby.

Battery and comfort: compare your normal day

Ask whether your preferred display, notifications and workouts fit between charges. Seller battery claims are not our measured runtime. For used stock, ask about battery condition and confirm the charging equipment is included. Check case size, strap fit and replacement-strap availability before choosing by colour or screen size.

Refurbished watches: check pairing and returns

Confirm the previous owner’s account lock has been removed, that the watch can pair normally and that its condition matches the description. Check warranty and returns before buying. Seller feedback can help assess the transaction, but does not establish the remaining battery life or the reliability of that particular watch.

eBay UK vs Amazon UK: where should you compare?

For Smartwatches, it is worth checking both retailers rather than assuming one is always cheaper. eBay UK can be useful for new, refurbished and open-box stock and exposes seller feedback clearly. Amazon UK can be useful for comparing new-stock availability, delivery options and retailer returns where offered. Always compare the exact model number, condition, warranty, delivery cost and returns policy before deciding.

How we choose these daily picks

Our product comparisons are built using current retailer data, market analysis and available marketplace feedback to identify the products most worthy of consideration. We do not rely on promotional messaging, manufacturer claims or advertised discounts when making recommendations. Instead, we focus on products that demonstrate strong value, positive seller signals and a credible marketplace track record. Although we have not physically tested every item featured, our methodology is designed to help consumers make informed and confident purchasing decisions. Where performance, safety or durability are especially important, we also encourage checking independent reviews of the exact model.

Buying questions answered

Can I use any smartwatch with an iPhone?

No. Check the manufacturer’s model-specific compatibility requirements. Pixel Watch does not support iPhone, and other brands vary.

Will an older Apple Watch work with my iPhone?

Check the watch model and installed watchOS against Apple’s table. Software updates can change which iPhone is required.

Is a cellular smartwatch worth paying extra for?

Consider it if you want supported calls or data away from the phone. Check carrier support and plan costs first.

What should I check on a refurbished smartwatch?

Check account-lock removal, battery condition, included charger, pairing, cosmetic condition, warranty and returns.
